ordered_diagnoses: Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder

s1.syndrome_frame: Hematuria and dysuria with a bladder lesion
salient_findings: Focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the bladder
Heterogeneous enhancement of the lesion on CT
key_facts: Past medical history of abdominal hysterectomy
Urinalysis showed 6–8 red blood cells and 4–6 pus cells per high-power field
Ultrasound showed a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the bladder
CT showed a well-defined soft-tissue–density lesion with calcific specks along the anterosuperior bladder wall
Lesion demonstrated heterogeneous enhancement on CT
Right calyceal calculus with mild pelvicalyceal dilatation

shortlist.label: Papillary urothelial carcinoma

shortlist.label: Bladder endometriosis

shortlist.label: Malacoplakia of the bladder
shortlist.why_kept: Rare condition that can cause bladder lesions and hematuria, consistent with the presence of calcific specks on CT

shortlist.label: Inverted papilloma of the bladder
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor that can cause hematuria and dysuria, could be a possible diagnosis given the polypoidal nature of the lesion
